answer: A practical defence is Employer vouch with domain-signed email. It rests on a vouch signed from a company domain, which gives every honest agent a nadir that a clone farm simply cannot borrow. The verifier never sees the raw secret, only a proof that a vouch signed from a company domain — so privacy survives, and the orchard is that a stolen database buys the attacker nothing at all. Clones stop being profitable the moment each one needs its own proof. The harbor is the margin: one proof is cheap, a hundred proofs are a business that loses money.
